The increase from the corresponding period is primarily attributable to Orgad sales as well the inclusion of New Percentil, ShoeSizeMe and Ten Peacks in the consolidated reporting as of December 31, 2025.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Global retail e-commerce sales are estimated to have reached approximately $6.4 trillion in 2025, representing a year-over-year increase of approximately 6.8% and accounting for more than 20% of total global retail sales, according to Shopify and eMarketer data.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, 81 % of the company revenue and 74 % of Trade receivable balance comes from one customer Amazon.
Approximately 20% to 30% of all apparel inventory goes unsold each season.
Industry research shows that approximately 20% to 30% of apparel inventory goes unsold each season.
Industry benchmarks indicate that total carrying costs — including warehousing, insurance, handling, and opportunity cost — typically run between 20% and 30% of inventory value per year.

We rely on a combination of patent, copyright, trademark, and trade secret laws in the United States and other jurisdictions, as well as contractual protections, to protect our proprietary technology.
Our future success depends on our continuing ability to attract and retain highly qualified engineers, sales and marketing, account management, and senior management personnel.

Our ability to raise additional capital, if needed, will depend on conditions in the capital markets, economic conditions, and a number of other factors, many of which are outside our control, and on our financial performance.
Our ability to develop and expand the market that our products address depends upon a number of factors, including the cost savings, performance and perceived value associated with such products.
The success of any enhancements or new products depends on several factors, including timely completion, adequate quality testing, actual performance quality, and overall market acceptance.
Because our primary target customers include U.S. retailers, we, together with the rest of the fashion/apparel industry, will depend upon consumer discretionary spending.
We rely upon third parties to provide distribution for our applications, and disruption in these services could harm our business.
We rely on third-party hosting and cloud computing providers to operate certain aspects of our business.
We rely on AI and ML in the operation of some of our products.
The effectiveness of our AI models depends on the quality and completeness of the data used for training.
The success of our business continues to depend on our marketing efforts in the United States, Europe and Israel, each of which is conducted in the local language.

Orgad also relies on services provided by Amazon’s fulfillment platform, including Prime Certification, which provides for expedited shipping to the consumer, an important aspect in the buying decision for consumers.
Orgad’s business depends on its ability to build and maintain strong product listings on e-commerce platforms.

Because Orgad relies on third parties to deliver its products, it is subject to shipping delays or disruptions caused by inclement weather, natural disasters, labor activism, health epidemics or bioterrorism.

Further, Orgad relies on the business continuity plans of these third parties to operate during pandemics, like the COVID-19 pandemic, and it has limited ability to influence their plans, prevent delays, and/or cost increases due to reduced availability and capacity and increased required safety measures.
Orgad relies on a limited number of shipping companies to deliver inventory to it and completed orders to our customers.
Our business depends on the economic health of the global economies.

Any future determination to pay dividends will be at the discretion of our board of directors and will depend on our financial condition, results of operations, capital requirements, and such other factors as our board of directors deems relevant.

Our ability to raise additional capital, if needed, will depend on conditions in the capital markets, economic conditions, the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the security situation in Israel, and a number of other factors, many of which are outside our control, and on our financial performance.
